user.title: Add a eufy account
user.description: Sign in with the eufy account that can see your HomeBase. Home Assistant keeps the signed-in session in a private store, so a restart does not sign in again.

data_description.email: The email address of the eufy account that owns the HomeBase, or of an account the home is shared with.
data_description.password: Used for this sign-in. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, so Home Assistant reuses the stored session afterwards instead of signing in again.
data_description.country: The country your eufy app signs in with (shown on its sign-in screen). eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Empty means Home Assistant's country.

reauth_confirm.title: Enter the eufy password again
reauth_confirm.description: eufy no longer accepts the saved sign-in for {account}: the password was rejected, none is saved, or eufy asks for a two-step verification code. Enter the current password, and Home Assistant signs in to eufy once to check it.

data_description.password: The current password of the eufy account. Repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours, so check it before submitting.

reauth_take_over.title: Sign the other client out of eufy?
reauth_take_over.description: Another app, device or integration is signed in with {account}. Continuing signs Home Assistant in to eufy and signs that other client out. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working meanwhile, so you can close this and try again later instead.

reconfigure.title: Sign in to eufy again
reconfigure.description: Home Assistant signs in to eufy once for {account} and keeps the new session. Use this after another app or device signed in with the account, after changing its password, or when the connection to eufy looks stale. Leave the password empty to sign in with the saved one. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, and repeated failed sign-ins lock it for 24 hours, so submit deliberately.

data_description.password: Optional. Leave empty to sign in with the saved password. Enter the account's current password to check it with eufy and save it in place of the old one.

verify_code.title: Enter the eufy verification code
verify_code.description: This eufy account uses two-step verification: eufy accepted the password and asks for the code it sends by e-mail. Enter the code to finish the sign-in. If no e-mail arrives, close this dialog and try again later; each attempt is a sign-in.

data_description.verify_code: The code from eufy's e-mail. Use the newest one if several arrived.

error.invalid_email: That is not an email address. Check it and try again; nothing was sent to eufy.
error.login_challenge: eufy wants a captcha for this sign-in. Sign in once in the eufy app on your phone, then try again here.
error.invalid_verify_code: eufy did not accept the code. Enter the newest code from eufy's e-mail; a new one may be on its way.
error.verification_refused: eufy did not accept the verification code and ended this sign-in. Sign in again to get a new code by e-mail, and enter it once. Repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours.
error.invalid_auth: eufy rejected the email or password; check both. Repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours.
error.login_limited: eufy is temporarily refusing sign-ins for this account. Wait before trying again: each attempt restarts the wait, and repeated attempts can lock the account for 24 hours.
error.session_replaced: Another app, device or integration signed in with this account and eufy ended the earlier session. Close that other client or wait, then try again.
error.session_rejected: eufy accepted the sign-in but then refused the session. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach eufy. Check the internet connection and try again.

abort.already_configured: This eufy account is already set up in Home Assistant.
abort.reauth_successful: eufy accepted the password. Home Assistant saved it and reloaded the account.
abort.reconfigure_successful: eufy accepted the sign-in. Home Assistant kept the session and reloaded the account.

init.title: eufy Home Security options
init.description: A change reloads the integration, except Sessions per HomeBase and Recording length, which apply at once.

detections.name: Detections and alarm
detections.description: The HomeBase announces a detection but never its end, and normally ends an alarm itself.

data.mode_holds_detections_repair: Repair when a security mode holds detections back

data_description.detection_hold: 5–300 s, 10 by default. A detection sensor turns off this long after the detection's own time. A detection that arrives after its hold has run out still fires its event.
data_description.alarm_timeout: 1–60 min, 10 by default. A safety net for an alarm whose end the HomeBase never reports: the panel then leaves Triggered or Pending, shows the guard mode last reported and reads it again.
data_description.mode_holds_detections_repair: On by default. A repair names the cameras whose Notification action is off in the armed security mode in force, so the station sends none of their individual detection notifications. Off removes these repairs and raises none; the cameras, the modes and their notifications are unchanged, and each camera's Detections in current mode sensor still shows it. Counter-derived Motion Activity and Recording Activity events may still work in these modes.

camera_activity.name: Camera activity polling
camera_activity.description: Use Motion Activity and Recording Activity events to trigger automations when new detection or recording activity is observed. These events use supported camera counters read locally, without requiring cloud push.

data_description.fast_activity_poll: Off by default: camera activity is checked during normal 45-second station polling. Enable this option to observe activity sooner on continuously connected stations. More frequent polling increases network traffic and CPU usage. On-demand stations retain their normal polling interval.
data_description.fast_activity_poll_interval: 1–44 seconds, 5 by default. Each poll reads the full station and paired-device parameter snapshot. Shorter intervals increase resource usage. One-second polling has been tested on a HomeBase 2 only; other models and firmware may behave differently.

camera_images.name: Camera images
camera_images.description: What a camera shows for a detection.

data.live_snapshot: Live snapshot for cameras without a detection image
data.full_resolution_capture: Capture live image at full resolution

data_description.camera_image: Thumbnail, then HD (default): the event's 640×360 thumbnail in about {thumbnail_seconds} s, then the first frame of its recording in about {hd_seconds} s plus decoding. Thumbnail only: never reads the recording. HD only: the recording's frame alone, so an event without a recording shows no image. Except with Thumbnail only, a HomeBase 2 event shows its recording's first frame once that recording has finished, with no thumbnail before it. Refresh event image follows this choice. None of them wakes a camera; Capture live image always does. After a change, cameras show no image until their next detection or button press.
data_description.refresh_keyframe: 1–5; 1 by default. Which keyframe of the HomeBase recording Refresh event image shows, unless Event image is Thumbnail only. A later keyframe can help when the first picture is dark or blurred, but the refresh takes longer and other cameras' images on the same HomeBase wait meanwhile. A recording with fewer keyframes uses its last one. The time between keyframes varies. Does not affect detection images, thumbnails or live captures, and never wakes the camera.
data_description.live_snapshot: Off by default. A camera with live video and no detection image yet shows one live picture instead, at most every 5 minutes. Wakes a battery camera, which costs battery.
data_description.full_resolution_capture: Off by default. Capture live image waits until the stream reaches the camera's full resolution and shows that picture, not the first, smaller one a woken camera sends. Takes longer, at most 30 s more, and keeps a battery camera awake that long, which costs battery. Image fetches for other cameras on the same HomeBase wait meanwhile.

data_description.station_sessions: {min_sessions}–{max_sessions}, {default_sessions} by default. Connections held to each HomeBase: one for detections and the first live view, one for event images, one more per further live view, so {default_live} cameras at once by default. A HomeBase holds about {max_sessions} across all apps and Home Assistant instances and drops one past that, the eufy app's included; give a second instance a small value such as 2. A live view past the limit waits briefly, then is refused. Ends no running live view.
data_description.record_length: 5–300 s, 30 by default. Length of a Record clip when the action names none. Wakes a battery camera for that long.

history.name: Event history
history.description: Images and videos are saved as files under {history_path}, a folder per camera; browse them under Media > My media.

data_description.event_history_days: 0–365, 7 by default. Saves every image a camera or preset shows, named with date, time, camera and what it shows. Older days are deleted; 0 saves nothing. In Home Assistant Container, mount a host directory at /media to keep them across updates.
data_description.event_videos: Off by default. Copies each recording a HomeBase makes from now on into the event history as an MP4, next to its image. Played from the HomeBase's storage, so no camera wakes. Needs Event history above 0 days; videos take far more space than images. Not for a camera without a HomeBase.

eufy_account.name: eufy account
eufy_account.description: Home Assistant reuses its saved eufy session; eufy allows only a few sign-ins per account per day.

data.session_probe: Check the eufy session every 6 hours

data_description.country: The country your eufy app signs in with (shown on its sign-in screen). eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Empty means Home Assistant's country. A change asks eufy once for the devices, which can cost a sign-in.
data_description.session_probe: On by default. A minute after start and every 6 hours, one device-list read with the saved session, never a sign-in. When another app or device has ended Home Assistant's session, the repair then shows within that time. Off: noticed at the next command that needs eufy or the next restart.
data_description.cloud_push: Off by default. Needed for individual detection notifications from a station that does not send them over the local network: a HomeBase 2, a camera without a HomeBase (such as a T8170 SoloCam) or a model not yet checked; a repair names each one. A HomeBase 3 sends its cameras' detections locally, and one that arrives both ways fires once. Home Assistant listens for eufy's push messages like the phone app, which keeps working. The messages pass through eufy's and Google's servers and can arrive late or not at all. Motion Activity and Recording Activity events use supported camera counters read locally and do not require cloud push.

more_countries.name: Extra countries (experimental)
more_countries.description: Experimental and little tested. Each extra country is one more sign-in to the account, on that country's eufy region: it can end Home Assistant's eufy session or the eufy app's, and it spends sign-ins from eufy's small daily limit. Use it only for a shared home that is otherwise missing, and remove it if the account keeps being signed out.

data.scan_regions: Look for devices under every sign-in country on each refresh

data_description.extra_countries: Empty by default. eufy lists a home shared with this account only to a sign-in with the country of the account that shared it. Add that country when it differs from the sign-in country. A change asks eufy once for the devices under every country.
data_description.scan_regions: Off by default. A sign-in country that listed no devices is not asked again. On: every device list asks each of them (Refresh device list, the session check, the hourly refresh for a camera without a HomeBase), so a device added later shows up; asking one whose session has run out signs in to it.

session_replaced.title: eufy ended Home Assistant's session for {account}

confirm.title: Sign Home Assistant in to eufy again
confirm.description: Another app, device or integration signed in with the eufy account {account}, and eufy ended Home Assistant's session; local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Home Assistant will sign in to eufy once with the saved password, which signs the other client out. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, so do this only when the other client is no longer needed. To avoid this for good, give Home Assistant its own eufy account, shared from the owner's account.

abort.login_failed: Signing in to eufy failed, so nothing changed and this repair stays open. Wait a while before trying again: repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours. You can also sign in again at any time with Reconfigure, on the account's menu under Settings > Devices & services.
abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Use Reconfigure on the account's menu under Settings > Devices & services, which signs in again whether or not the account is loaded, or wait until it has finished loading and open this repair again.

login_limited.title: eufy is refusing sign-ins for {account}
login_limited.description: eufy is refusing sign-ins for the eufy account {account}. The next sign-in is allowed after {time}. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Do not sign in sooner, in Home Assistant or elsewhere: each early attempt can restart the wait. This notice clears at that time, or when Home Assistant next starts the integration without needing a sign-in.

login_limited_no_wait.title: eufy is refusing sign-ins for {account}
login_limited_no_wait.description: eufy is temporarily refusing sign-ins for the eufy account {account}. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Wait before signing in again, in Home Assistant or elsewhere: each early attempt can restart the wait. This notice clears when Home Assistant next starts the integration without needing a sign-in.

login_budget.title: Home Assistant is holding back eufy sign-ins for {account}
login_budget.description: Home Assistant has used its own limit of {budget} sign-ins per {window_hours} hours on the eufy cluster that serves the sign-in country {country} of the eufy account {account}; eufy itself refused nothing. The next sign-in is allowed after {time}. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Every sign-in country on that cluster, extra countries included, counts against this limit. This notice clears at that time, or when Home Assistant next starts the integration without needing a sign-in.

confirm.title: Allow one more key fetch for {station}
confirm.description: {station} rejects its key, even after Home Assistant fetched the key from eufy again once, so its entities are unavailable; Home Assistant does not fetch the key again by itself. Confirm to reload the eufy account and allow one more key fetch, for example after the station was reset or moved to another account. If it still rejects the key, this repair comes back.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account or this station is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Wait until it has finished loading, then open this repair again.
abort.reset_failed: Home Assistant could not allow another key fetch, so nothing changed and this repair stays open. Try again later.

credentials_refreshed.title: Fetched the key for {station} again
credentials_refreshed.description: {station} rejected its old key, so Home Assistant fetched its key or owner id from eufy again. No sign-in was needed. You can dismiss this notice.

credentials_refreshed_login.title: Fetched the key for {station} again, with a sign-in
credentials_refreshed_login.description: {station} rejected its old key, so Home Assistant fetched its key or owner id from eufy again. This cost one eufy sign-in, and eufy limits how often an account may sign in. You can dismiss this notice.

account_id_mismatch.title: {station} stamps its events with another eufy account
account_id_mismatch.description: The HomeBase {station} stamps its records with an owner account other than the one Home Assistant sends with its commands, so it may silently ignore arming, disarming and setting changes. Home Assistant has not changed anything and never adopts another account on its own. Check that this eufy account owns the HomeBase or is a member it serves, then reload the integration; the check runs again after a reload.

media_not_persistent.title: Camera event history is not kept across container updates
media_not_persistent.description: Camera images are saved to {path}, but nothing is mounted there, so they are lost when the Home Assistant container is recreated or updated. Mount a directory of the host at /media, for example `- /srv/homeassistant/media:/media` under `volumes:` in docker-compose.yaml, and recreate the container. To stop saving images instead, set Event history to 0 in the integration's options.

push_not_running.title: eufy cloud push is not running for {account}
push_not_running.description: Cloud push is switched on for the eufy account {account}, but Home Assistant is not receiving eufy's push messages right now. Until it is, individual detection notifications from stations that do not send them locally (a HomeBase 2, a camera without a HomeBase), and changes made in the eufy app, arrive late or not at all. Local control and individual detection notifications from a HomeBase 3 keep working. Motion Activity and Recording Activity events can still report increases in supported camera counters read locally, without cloud push. Home Assistant keeps retrying by itself, and this notice clears when push runs again. If it stays, check that Home Assistant can reach the internet, and look at the log for the reason. To stop using cloud push, switch it off in the integration's options.

push_needed.title: eufy detection notifications need cloud push for {account}

confirm.title: Switch on cloud push
confirm.description: These stations of the eufy account {account} do not send their cameras' individual detection notifications over the local network: {stations}. Their conventional detection sensors and events require cloud push. Motion Activity and Recording Activity events can still report increases in supported camera counters read locally, without cloud push. Confirm to switch on Cloud push for detections in the integration's options: Home Assistant reloads the eufy account and then listens for eufy's push messages, which pass through eufy's and Google's servers. To leave it off, ignore this repair; it is checked again on every reload.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Wait until it has finished loading, then open this repair again.

lan_reply_blocked.title: eufy stations on this network connect through eufy's servers for {account}

recordings_pin_protected.title: Some recordings of {camera} cannot be saved
recordings_pin_protected.description: Some recordings of {camera_markdown} are protected by the eufy app's Local Advanced Encryption, so Home Assistant cannot save or play them. They stay on the HomeBase and play in the eufy app. To have new recordings saved here, turn off Local Advanced Encryption in the eufy app under Settings > Security > Media Content Encryption. Recordings made while it was on stay encrypted.

mode_holds_detections.title: {station}: detection notifications off for some cameras in {mode} mode
mode_holds_detections.description: In {mode} mode the station sends no individual detection notifications for {devices}: their Notification action is off in this mode, so Home Assistant gets no individual motion or person notifications from them until a mode that sends them is in force ({sending_modes}). Motion Activity and Recording Activity events can still report increases in supported camera counters read locally, even with Notification switched off. To receive individual detection notifications in {mode}, open the eufy app → Security mode → {mode} → each camera, and turn on Notification (this also notifies your phone). Ignore this if you keep {mode} silent on purpose. To stop these repairs for every mode, switch off the option Repair when a security mode holds detections back (the integration → Configure).

mode_holds_detections_nowhere.title: {station}: detection notifications off for some cameras in {mode} mode
mode_holds_detections_nowhere.description: In {mode} mode the station sends no individual detection notifications for {devices}: their Notification action is off in this mode, so Home Assistant gets no individual motion or person notifications from them in any armed mode the station reports. Motion Activity and Recording Activity events can still report increases in supported camera counters read locally, even with Notification switched off. To receive individual detection notifications in {mode}, open the eufy app → Security mode → {mode} → each camera, and turn on Notification (this also notifies your phone). Ignore this if you keep {mode} silent on purpose. To stop these repairs for every mode, switch off the option Repair when a security mode holds detections back (the integration → Configure).

cipher_unavailable.title: eufy has no key for {station}
cipher_unavailable.description: {station} uses key number {cipher} for its local connection, but eufy holds no such key for the station's owner, so Home Assistant cannot connect to it and its entities are unavailable. Signing in again does not help. In the eufy app, on the account that set the station up, check that the station is still there and shared with the account Home Assistant uses; share it again if needed. Then reload the integration: Home Assistant asks eufy again on every reload, and on its own at most once an hour.

cipher_key_missing.title: eufy sends no key for {station}
cipher_key_missing.description: {station} uses key number {cipher} for its local connection. eufy answers for that key number but without the key itself, so Home Assistant cannot connect to it and its entities are unavailable. Signing in again does not help. Home Assistant asks eufy again on every reload, and on its own at most once an hour. If it stays, please open an issue with the integration's diagnostics download.

key_unusable.title: eufy serves no usable key for {station}
key_unusable.description: {station} needs a key for its connection method that eufy does not serve for it, so Home Assistant cannot connect to it and its entities are unavailable. Fetching the key again returns the same, and signing in again does not help. Please open an issue with the integration's diagnostics download.

no_devices.title: No eufy devices found for {account}
no_devices.description: The eufy account {account} lists no devices ({regions}), so Home Assistant has nothing to set up. Home Assistant does not ask again by itself. Check in the eufy app that the account sees the HomeBase or camera; a shared account sees only what the owner shared with it, and only after it accepted the invitation. Check that the integration's eufy sign-in country (in its options) is the country your eufy app signs in with, and add the country of anyone who shared a home with this account as an extra sign-in country: eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Changing a country asks eufy again. Otherwise turn on Look for devices under every sign-in country on each refresh and press Refresh device list on the eufy account device; you can turn it off again once the devices show.

variant_reset.title: Some eufy settings show extra copies

confirm.title: Remove the extra copies of eufy settings
confirm.description:
These devices show some settings more than once, under the same name:

{devices}

The eufy app uses only one copy of each setting. The other copies may not work.

Submit to disable the extra copies ({disable} in total). Nothing is deleted: you can enable a copy again later under Settings → Devices & services → Entities (choose to show disabled entities in the filter). Copies you enabled or disabled yourself stay as they are.

To keep everything as it is, ignore this repair.

confirm_swap.title: Fix the copies of eufy settings
confirm_swap.description:
On these devices, some settings show copies the eufy app does not use:

{devices}

Those copies may not work, and for some settings the copy the eufy app uses is disabled.

Submit to disable the copies the eufy app does not use ({disable} in total) and enable the copies it uses ({enable} in total). Nothing is deleted. The eufy account then reloads, which can take about a minute. Copies you enabled or disabled yourself stay as they are.

To keep everything as it is, ignore this repair.

confirm_enable.title: Turn the eufy settings back on
confirm_enable.description:
Some settings the eufy app uses are disabled on these devices:

{devices}

Submit to enable those settings ({enable} in total). The eufy account then reloads, which can take about a minute. Settings you disabled yourself stay as they are.

To keep everything as it is, ignore this repair.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is still loading. Open this repair again when it is ready.
abort.nothing_to_reset: Nothing to fix: each setting is shown once, or you chose the copies yourself.

accept.title: Accept the eufy invitation
accept.description:
**{invitation}** for the eufy account {account}.

Submit to accept it. After the last one, Home Assistant reloads the eufy account to load the shared devices.

accept_code.title: Accept the eufy invitation
accept_code.description:
**{invitation}** for the eufy account {account}.

Enter the code that came with the invitation and submit. After the last one, Home Assistant reloads the eufy account to load the shared devices.

data_description.code: Sent with the invitation by the person who shared it.

confirm.title: Load the shared devices
confirm.description: Home Assistant finds no open invitation for the eufy account {account}. Submit, and Home Assistant reloads the account and asks eufy for its devices.

error.wrong_code: That code does not open this invitation, so nothing was sent to eufy. Check the code with the person who sent the invitation.
error.code_missing: This invitation needs the code that came with it.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Wait until it has finished loading, then open this repair again.
abort.accept_in_app: Home Assistant cannot accept **{invitation}**. Accept it in the eufy app signed in with this account, then open this repair again to load the devices.
abort.session_lapsed: Home Assistant's eufy session for this invitation's region had ended, so the invitation was not accepted. Home Assistant reloads the eufy account to sign in there again; then open this repair again.
abort.accept_failed: eufy did not accept the invitation, or could not be reached. Try again later, or accept it in the eufy app signed in with this account.
abort.session_replaced: Another app, device or integration signed in with this eufy account and eufy ended Home Assistant's session, so the invitation was not accepted. Sign Home Assistant in again with the repair "eufy ended Home Assistant's session" or Reconfigure, then open this repair again.

station_webrtc_only.title: eufy station needs WebRTC for {account}
station_webrtc_only.description: The eufy account {account} lists a station the eufy app reaches only over its WebRTC connection, which this integration does not support yet: {devices} (the station and the devices paired to it). They are left out; the account's other stations work as usual. This repair is checked again on every reload and on Refresh device list.

station_p2p_id_unsupported.title: eufy station not supported for {account}
station_p2p_id_unsupported.description: The eufy account {account} lists a station whose P2P id local connections do not accept: {devices}. The eufy app does not connect to it locally either, so Home Assistant leaves it and the devices paired to it out; the account's other stations work as usual. Nothing in Home Assistant can change that. This repair is checked again on every reload and on Refresh device list.

device_serial_unsupported.title: eufy device not supported for {account}
device_serial_unsupported.description: The eufy account {account} lists a device whose serial number is not only letters and digits: {devices}. Home Assistant cannot name it, so it leaves it out (and, for a station, the devices paired to it); the account's other devices work as usual. This repair is checked again on every reload and on Refresh device list. If the device shows in the eufy app, open an issue with the diagnostics download.

auth_failed.message: eufy rejected the saved password for this account, or none is saved. Re-enter it in the reauthentication dialog; Home Assistant will not try the old password again.

guard_mode_not_applied.message: {station} took the change to {target} but did not apply it. The panel shows the mode {station} last reported. If this keeps happening, check in the eufy app that {station} is shared with this eufy account.

guard_mode_rejected.message: {station} refused {target}. The panel shows the mode {station} last reported.

guard_mode_command_unsupported.message: {station} answered that it does not support {target}. The panel shows the mode {station} last reported; change the mode in the eufy app.

guard_mode_not_supported.message: Home Assistant cannot switch {station} to {target}: the eufy library does not set the guard mode of this model, so nothing was sent. Change the mode in the eufy app.

setting_not_applied.message: {station} took the change to {target} but did not apply it. The entity shows the value {station} last reported; check that the device is online and try again.

setting_rejected.message: {station} refused the change to {target}. The entity shows the value {station} last reported.

setting_command_unsupported.message: {station} answered that the device does not support changing {target}. The entity shows the value {station} last reported.

account_rejected.message: {station} refused {target}: it does not accept this eufy account. Check in the eufy app that {station} is shared with this eufy account; trying again changes nothing until it is.

setting_device_unavailable.message: The device {target} belongs to cannot be addressed, so nothing was sent and the entity still shows the value the HomeBase last reported. eufy's device list does not pair it to this HomeBase, or names no slot for it. If the device was removed or re-paired, reload the integration; otherwise check that it is still paired in the eufy app.

setting_unconfirmed.message: The device did not confirm the change to {target} in time. It may still apply: the entity shows unknown until the next update shows the value in force.

setting_value_invalid.message: {target} does not accept this value, so nothing was sent. Choose a value the setting allows: a number must sit on one of its steps from the minimum, as the slider offers.

light_control_off.message: {target} was not switched, and nothing was sent: the eufy app turns the lamp's control off while {setting} is off. Turn {setting} on first, in the eufy app or with its switch here.

station_unreachable.message: The station did not answer, so {target} was not set. Home Assistant keeps reconnecting; check that it is powered on and reachable, on this network or through eufy's servers.

on_demand_unreachable.message: The camera did not answer, so {target} was not set. A battery camera sleeps between commands and takes about ten seconds to wake; check that it is charged and within Wi-Fi range and that Home Assistant can reach eufy's servers, then try again.

session_replaced_see_repairs.message: Another app or device signed in with the eufy account and ended Home Assistant's session, so {target} was not set. Waking a battery camera needs a key from eufy, which refuses the ended session. Open the account's repair under Settings > System > Repairs to sign in again, or use Reconfigure on the account entry; Home Assistant does not sign in again by itself.

station_key_rejected.message: The station rejected its key, so {target} was not set. Open its repair under Settings > System > Repairs to let Home Assistant fetch its key once more.

station_key_unusable.message: eufy serves no key this station can use, so {target} was not set. See its repair under Settings > System > Repairs.

cloud_unavailable.message: Changing {target} needed the HomeBase's key fetched from eufy again, and eufy could not be reached or is temporarily refusing this account, so it was not set. Check Settings > System > Repairs for this account and try again later; Home Assistant does not sign in again by itself.

cache_unavailable.message: The eufy account's cached device list is not available, and eufy cannot be reached right now. Home Assistant retries setting it up.

device_list_refresh_failed.message: The device list could not be fetched from eufy, so nothing changed. Check Settings > System > Repairs for this account and try again later.

capture_in_progress.message: The camera is busy taking another image, so nothing was sent. A capture takes about ten seconds; try again after it.

preset_not_set.message: Preset {index} is not set on this camera, so nothing was sent. Set it in the eufy app, then press Refresh presets.

presets_unsupported.message: This camera has no pan/tilt presets, so nothing was sent.

preset_image_unsupported.message: This camera cannot take a picture of a preset, so nothing was sent.

default_preset_needs_confirmation.message: The camera asks to confirm before making this preset its default, so nothing was changed. Choose the default preset in the eufy app, then press Refresh presets.

pan_tilt_not_applied.message: The camera did not take the pan/tilt step, so it did not move. It may still be turning from the last command; wait a few seconds and try again.

pan_tilt_unsupported.message: This camera cannot pan, tilt or zoom, so nothing was sent.

zoom_unsupported.message: This camera has no zoom, so nothing was sent.

ptz_command_not_handled.message: The HomeBase refused this camera command as one it does not handle, so the camera did not change. Trying again will not help.

zoom_needs_single_view.message: The camera zooms only in single view, so nothing was sent. Switch it to single view in the eufy app, then try again.

presets_full.message: All {slots} preset slots are in use; delete a preset first. Nothing was saved.

preset_not_saved.message: The camera did not save the view as a preset. It may still be turning from the last command; wait a few seconds and try again.

preset_saved_not_default.message: The view was saved as a preset, but the camera did not make it its default. Choose it in Default preset to try again.

preset_not_deleted.message: The camera still holds preset {index}, so it was not deleted. Wait a few seconds and try again.

preset_slot_unknown.message: This camera has no preset slot {index}, so nothing was sent.

preset_save_unsupported.message: This camera cannot save a view as a preset, so nothing was sent.

preset_delete_unsupported.message: This camera cannot delete a preset, so nothing was sent.

preset_default_unsupported.message: This camera cannot change its default preset, so nothing was sent.

preset_image_invalid.message: The preset picture is not a JPEG image of at most {max_mb} MB, so it was not stored.

recording_in_progress.message: This camera is already recording a clip, so no second one was started. Wait for the running clip to finish, then try again.

recording_needs_history.message: Clips are saved in the event history, which is off. Set Event history to 1 day or more in the integration's options, then try again.

recording_unsupported.message: This camera has no live stream in Home Assistant, so it cannot record a clip.

live_stream_limit.message: The HomeBase has no session free for another live stream: the sessions per HomeBase option allows {limit} at once and none ended in time. Close another live view of this HomeBase, or raise the option, then try again.

camera_unavailable.message: The camera sent no picture, so no clip was saved. A battery camera sleeps between uses and takes a few seconds to wake; check that it is charged and within Wi-Fi range, then try again.

recording_not_running.message: This camera is not recording a clip, so there is nothing to stop.

recording_stopped_empty.message: The recording was stopped before the camera sent its first picture, so no clip was saved.

recording_failed.message: The camera sent the clip, but Home Assistant could not save it to the event history. Check that the media folder is writable and has free space, and that Home Assistant's ffmpeg works; the log has the details.

security_mode_not_settable.message: Home Assistant cannot switch the HomeBase to {mode}, so nothing was sent. Choose another mode, or set this one in the eufy app.

siren_not_confirmed.message: The device acknowledged the request for {target} but did not confirm it, so it may or may not be sounding. Check the device and try again.

siren_rejected.message: The device refused the request for {target}, so it did not change. Check in the eufy app that the device is online, then try again.

siren_account_rejected.message: {station} refused the request for {target}: it does not accept this eufy account. Check in the eufy app that {station} is shared with this eufy account; trying again changes nothing until it is.

siren_unsupported.message: Home Assistant cannot use {target}: the eufy app offers no such alarm for this device, or eufy's device list no longer pairs it to its station. Nothing was sent; after changing devices in the eufy app, use Refresh device list.

siren_duration_invalid.message: The HomeBase siren sounds for at most {max} seconds. Choose a duration of {max} seconds or less.

lock_not_writable.message: Home Assistant cannot lock or unlock this lock: {reason}. Nothing was sent; use the eufy app.

lock_command_waiting.message: The lock's last command is still waiting for the lock to report its state, so nothing was sent. Try again when it has.

lock_guest.message: The eufy account is a guest of this lock, and eufy gives guests no lock or unlock, so nothing was sent. Use the eufy app with the owner's account.

lock_mqtt_required.message: This lock takes its commands over eufy's MQTT broker, and this install lacks the MQTT client the integration requires (the log says so), so nothing was sent. Install the integration again, or use the eufy app.

lock_unsupported.message: eufy's device list or sign-in gives this account no lock control of this lock yet, so nothing was sent. Use the eufy app.

lock_device_busy.message: Another command for this lock is still waiting for the lock, so nothing was sent. Try again when the lock has reported its state.

lock_command_rejected.message: The lock or its station refused the command (code {code}); the lock did not move for it.

lock_not_moved.message: The lock took the command but then reported {state}: the bolt may be stuck. Check the lock.

lock_timeout.message: The lock did not report the asked state in time; check the lock. Its next report shows whether it moved.

lock_unreachable.message: The lock, its station or eufy's broker could not be reached, so the command was not confirmed; try again in a moment. The lock's next report shows whether it moved.

lock_command_failed.message: The lock command failed and was not confirmed. The lock's next report shows whether it moved.

lock_session_replaced.message: Another app or device signed in with the eufy account and ended Home Assistant's session, so the lock command was not sent. Open the account's repair under Settings > System > Repairs to sign in again, or use Reconfigure on the account entry; Home Assistant does not sign in again by itself.

lock_cloud_unavailable.message: The lock command needed eufy's servers (the lock's key or the connection for its commands), and eufy could not be reached or refused this account, so it was not sent. Check Settings > System > Repairs for this account and try again later.

lock_key_rejected.message: The lock's station rejected its key, so the lock command was not sent. Open the station's repair under Settings > System > Repairs to let Home Assistant fetch its key once more.

lock_key_unusable.message: eufy serves no key the lock's station can use, so the lock command was not sent. See the station's repair under Settings > System > Repairs.

lock_command_cancelled.message: The lock command was stopped because the eufy account entry was unloaded, before the lock reported its state. Check the lock.

garage_door_position_unknown.message: The garage door's position is unknown. Use the eufy app to move it.

garage_door_moving.message: The garage door is still moving. Try again when it has stopped.

garage_other_door_moving.message: The other garage door on this camera is still moving. Try again when it has stopped.

capture_preset.name: Capture preset image
capture_preset.description: Turns a pan/tilt camera to one of its preset positions and takes a live image of that view, shown by that preset's image entity. Wakes a battery camera and leaves it at the preset.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

pan_tilt.name: Pan or tilt
pan_tilt.description: Moves a pan/tilt camera one fixed step, as its Pan and Tilt buttons do. Wakes a battery camera; it returns to its default preset once idle.

goto_preset.name: Go to preset
goto_preset.description: Turns a pan/tilt camera to one of its preset positions once, without taking an image. Wakes a battery camera; it returns to its default preset once idle. The live view preset is not changed.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

zoom.name: Zoom
zoom.description: Zooms the live view one step in or out, as the Live view zoom slider does. With a live view open the camera zooms at once; otherwise the next live view opens at that zoom.

save_preset.name: Save preset
save_preset.description: Stores what a pan/tilt camera shows now as a preset: in its lowest free slot, or over the given one. Use it while the live view runs, or within a few seconds of the last pan or tilt: the camera returns to its default view a few seconds after the last move. Returns the slot index when a response is asked for.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: Overwrite this slot instead of taking the lowest free one; the first slot is 0.

make_default.name: Make default
make_default.description: Also make the saved preset the one the camera returns to when idle; the camera turns there.

delete_preset.name: Delete preset
delete_preset.description: Clears one preset slot of a pan/tilt camera. Its entities go unavailable; deleting the default preset leaves the camera without one until another is chosen.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

record.name: Record clip
record.description: Records a clip of the camera's live stream and saves it as an MP4 in the event history, next to the camera's images. Wakes a battery camera for the clip's length. Shares a running live view instead of opening a second stream. Returns the saved file's media id, its length and whether it is complete when a response is asked for.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Seconds to record, from 5 to 300. Without it, the Recording length option is used.

stop_recording.name: Stop recording
stop_recording.description: Ends the clip the camera is recording now. The part recorded so far is saved in the event history as a complete clip, and the Record clip action returns.
